questions.q: What does a VLAN (virtual LAN) do?
options: Logically divides one physical network into separate broadcast domains through switch configuration
Physically separates devices by running entirely new cabling for each group
Encrypts all traffic between devices on the network
Increases the maximum speed of a network connection
questions.explain: VLANs split a physical network into multiple logical broadcast domains without requiring separate physical cabling.

options: The set of devices that receive each other's broadcast traffic
A list of all approved firewall rules on a network
A single physical cable connecting two switches
The range of public IP addresses owned by an organization
questions.explain: Devices in the same broadcast domain all receive each other's broadcast traffic by default.

questions.q: What does 802.1Q tagging do on a trunk link between switches?
options: Inserts a tag into each Ethernet frame identifying which VLAN it belongs to
Encrypts the frame so other VLANs cannot read it
Physically splits the trunk cable into separate wires per VLAN
Removes the need for VLANs entirely
questions.explain: 802.1Q tags each frame with its VLAN membership so a single shared trunk link can correctly carry multiple VLANs.

questions.q: Why are IoT devices commonly placed in their own isolated VLAN?
options: They often ship with weak default credentials and rarely receive security updates, making them a common entry point for attackers
IoT devices cannot physically connect to a VLAN-enabled switch
IoT devices generate more broadcast traffic than any other device type
Placing IoT devices on their own VLAN is purely a performance optimization
questions.explain: IoT devices are often poorly secured, so isolating them limits what an attacker can reach if one is compromised.

questions.q: What is the core goal of a role-and-risk-based network segmentation strategy?
options: Ensuring a compromise that starts in one segment doesn't automatically spread into every other segment
Making every device on the network reachable from every other device for convenience
Eliminating the need for firewalls between any segments
Guaranteeing that no device can ever be compromised
questions.explain: Segmentation groups devices by role and risk so that a breach in one segment is contained rather than spreading network-wide.
